provider: iiif.archive.org (free IIIF Image API over any uploaded image)

free_tier.stated: No separate quota. It is a free image server over items you already hold, one image per item. Capacity therefore follows the 1TB/item rule.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: 1TB size limit for item pages; recommended maximum 1000 files or 500GB per item. The IIIF workshop page separately advises uploading one image per item to avoid viewer problems.

retention.stated: Items uploaded as test items are removed after approximately 30 days; no removal term for other items is stated.
retention.notes: Only test items are removed, after approximately 30 days (the Internet Archive help page describes the Test Collection/Test Item feature; the IIIF workshop page says the 30-day delete is useful when testing). No retention term for other items is stated on either page.

egress.terms: Free, and it is a rendering endpoint, so one stored master serves arbitrary region/size/rotation/quality requests. The cheapest possible way to serve image bytes at many sizes.

tooling: IIIF Image API v2 and v3 (Cantaloupe server); any IIIF viewer or plain GET on /iiif/<identifier>/info.json; no rclone backend
chaining: Allows storing high-resolution master images and serving rendered image tiles or thumbnails via IIIF endpoints, reducing outbound transfer bandwidth across requests.
limits_note: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.

extras.quota_verbatim: No separate quota — it is a free image server over items you already hold, one image per item. Capacity therefore follows the 1TB/item rule.
extras.limits_verbatim: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free, and it is a rendering endpoint, so one stored master serves arbitrary region/size/rotation/quality requests — the cheapest possible way to serve image bytes at many sizes
extras.chaining_verbatim: Store one large master per item, then let clients request tiles/thumbnails instead of originals — cuts served bytes by orders of magnitude for an image-heavy 500GB-1TiB/day workload. Multiply by unlimited items.
extras.tooling_verbatim: IIIF Image API v2 and v3 (Cantaloupe server); any IIIF viewer or plain GET on /iiif/<identifier>/info.json; no rclone backend
extras.agent_focus: Internet Archive deep dive: IAS3 S3-like API, per-item unlimited size, upload API, metadata, derivatives, CDX, the web archive as a CDN, practical throughput/rate limits for 20TB

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
